answer: A tier-3 answer must contain at least 7 distinct claims, each naming a different term from the published vocabulary, and the count is taken before grading. Since the harbor tally is stored with the zenith verdict, the beacon audit can re-derive it and a padded answer publishes the same claim repeated. A farm padding one paragraph thus cannot reach the threshold however long it makes the text, because length is not what is counted. That is 7 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
